blocks.content: Proposed by H.F. Reid after the 1906 San Francisco earthquake, the Elastic Rebound Theory explains that tectonic stress gradually deforms rocks on either side of a fault. When the stress surpasses rock strength, the rocks snap back to their original position, releasing stored energy.

items: H.F. Reid is frequently asked in exams as the scientist who proposed the Elastic Rebound Theory.
The theory was formulated based on observations from the 1906 San Francisco earthquake.
Earthquake energy release occurs precisely when tectonic stress surpasses rock strength.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Elastic Rebound Theory was proposed by H.F. Reid following the 1906 San Francisco earthquake.
Tectonic stress gradually deforms rocks along either side of a geological fault line.
When accumulated stress exceeds the strength of the rock, it snaps back into place, releasing stored energy.
